title: Impulse
body:
**Impulse** is the change in momentum produced by a force acting over an interval of time.

$$
J = F\,\Delta t = \Delta p
$$

The equation says that a given change in momentum can be produced by a large force over a short
time or a small force over a long one, which is the design principle behind every safety device
in a vehicle.

```
A 70 kg passenger at 15 m/s is brought to rest.
  Δp = 70 × 15 = 1050 kg·m/s, whatever the details

  stopped in 0.05 s (rigid dashboard):   F = 1050/0.05 = 21,000 N
  stopped in 0.30 s (airbag):            F =  1050/0.30 = 3,500 N
```

The momentum change is fixed by the collision, so the only variable available is the time, and
a crumple zone, an airbag and a helmet liner all buy time. The same reasoning explains bending
your knees when landing and following through when catching a ball.

For a force that varies during the impact, the impulse is the [[Integral]] of force over time,
which is the area under the force-time curve.
